ledger: Wind: no evidence of wind at any point; trees, foliage and the loose black T-shirt show no fluttering; clouds static apart from camera motion. Nothing implies airflow, and nothing reacts as if there were any, so this is consistent.
Skater forward motion (rolling 00:00-01:25, 03:50-07:75, 09:50-09:75): T-shirt and baggy trousers hang naturally with no streaming. This is consistent with low rolling speed.

Gravity, trick 1 (pop at ~01:25-01:45, airborne to ~03:20, rolling away at 03:50): rider and board leave the ground and stay airborne about 1.7-1.8 s. Between ~01:70 and ~02:75 the rider stays at nearly the same screen height relative to a stable tree/horizon line, with little visible rise or fall arc. The board hovers below the feet at a constant offset.

Gravity, trick 2 (pop ~08:00, airborne 08:25-09:25, landing 09:50): airborne about 1.25 s over the bowl edge. The rider moves up and then down through the frames. This is plausible-ish for a transfer, and the shadow on the ground at 09:00-09:25 is detached from the rider, which is consistent with being airborne.

Sunlight/shadows: the sun appears high behind the rider at 01:25-03:50, and hard ground shadows fall toward or left of the camera at 00:00-00:75 and 04:00-07:75. Shadow direction stays consistent with the sun as the camera rotates, and the shadow is present and attached while the rider is rolling.
Shirt lift at 03:50 and 09:50-09:75 (skin at the waist): explained by the arm raised overhead and the body bending, not by wind. Consistent.

findings.entity: skater and skateboard during first aerial trick
findings.description: After the pop at ~01:25-01:45, rider and board stay airborne until ~03:20, about 1.75 s, which implies a jump apex of several metres. Yet the rider is never shown far above the coping. From ~01:70 to ~02:75 the rider keeps nearly the same screen height relative to the stable treeline/horizon (the camera is not visibly tracking upward), so the arc looks flat and floaty. The board hovers at a fixed distance below the feet without the expected fall. Gravity appears weakened during this aerial.

actual_input_modality: timestamped JPEG frames viewed with the Read tool, grouped six per contact sheet; original video available for denser extraction
